answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits prove fraud. A whisper of suspiciously coordinated outputs can trigger extra audits, but reputation alone should not convict: evidence must tie the breach to the locked bond. Spawning a thousand sybils then costs a thousand funded stakes, and detected cheating burns them, making the attack expensive even in the tundra of cheap compute; the zenith is not perfect prevention, but raising the price of abuse.
